veranderings.voor: wat jy kan uitgooi soos meel

veranderings.rede: The comparison sits more naturally before the verb cluster in an Afrikaans subordinate clause.

veranderings.voor: strooi die poeier stadig daarby in
veranderings.na: strooi die poeier stadig daarin
veranderings.rede: 'daarby in' is an awkward combination; 'daarin' says plainly that the powder goes into the water.

veranderings.voor: Die roer maak van die twee een dik pap sonder klonte.
veranderings.na: Deur te roer word die twee een dik pap sonder klonte.
veranderings.rede: The nominalised 'Die roer' as subject is stiff and can be misread; a verbal construction reads more naturally.

veranderings.voor: bly nie lank sag nie en dit word hard
veranderings.na: bly nie lank sag nie, en dit word hard
veranderings.rede: AWS 2017: comma before 'en' joining two clauses that each have their own subject and verb.

veranderings.voor: fyn droë poeier
veranderings.na: fyn, droë poeier
veranderings.rede: Two coordinate adjectives that each describe the noun are separated by a comma.

veranderings.voor: Die pap gaan tussen planke en dit verhard
veranderings.na: Die pap gaan tussen planke in, en dit verhard
veranderings.rede: 'gaan tussen planke' needs 'in' to complete the movement, and AWS requires a comma before 'en' joining two full clauses.

veranderings.voor: droog en los en dit loop
veranderings.na: droog en los, en dit loop
veranderings.rede: AWS 2017: comma before 'en' joining two clauses with their own subject and verb; it also separates the clause 'en' from the list 'en'.

veranderings.voor: soveel water as meel by en jy kry
veranderings.na: soveel water as meel by, en jy kry
veranderings.rede: AWS 2017: comma before 'en' joining two clauses that each have their own verb (and here a new subject).

veranderings.voor: Die pasta is taai en dit plak
veranderings.na: Die pasta is taai, en dit plak

veranderings.voor: Die meng alleen maak dus reeds 'n gom.
veranderings.na: Net deur te meng kry jy dus reeds 'n gom.
veranderings.rede: The nominal subject 'Die meng alleen' is wooden; a verbal phrase keeps the same meaning (mixing only, nothing more) and reads naturally.

veranderings.voor: meel verdwyn en 'n mens hou

veranderings.blok: Wat verander en wat bly dieselfde
veranderings.voor: Jellie is na die tyd nog nat
veranderings.na: Jellie is daarna nog nat
veranderings.rede: 'na die tyd' echoes English 'after the time'; 'daarna' is the standard Afrikaans word with the same meaning.

veranderings.blok: Wat verander en wat bly dieselfde
veranderings.voor: voor en na die meng
veranderings.na: voor en ná die meng
veranderings.rede: The accent on 'ná' marks the time meaning 'after', set against 'voor', as AWS allows for clarity.

vlae.teks: Met water word die poeier weer hard.
vlae.rede: Read on its own, the entry never names a powder before 'die poeier'; the first sentence only implies it through 'fyn te maal'. Making the link explicit would mean adding wording to the definition, so this is left for the reviewer or writer.
